Please see below and let me know your thoughts as soon 
as possible... 
Aspen the town — or Snowmass? Snowmass is the major 
'Aspen ski resort' — Aspen is the town. Snowmass is about 20 
minutes away on convenient shuttle. With more ski in and 
out options. Most stay at Snowmass, then go to Aspen for 
shopping and dining. The ski hill in Aspen is smaller and 
steeper. If they are expert to intermediate skiers and are 
familiar with this type of terrain, then Aspen might be 
perfect. Otherwise I might recommend Snowmass. 
Lift ticket passes work for both Aspen, Snowmass and the two 
smaller hills in-between called Highlands and Buttermilk. But 
Snowmass is by far the larger ski area base with three village 
levels of shopping and dining. 
Rentals can be picked up at a conveniently located shop or 
delivered at the lodge. Skiers or snowboarders? Helmets or 
no helmets?

A message from SAXE MIDDLE SCHOOL 
How is Saxe doing in this time of heightened concern 
around student/school safety? 
It is a credit to our families and to the Saxe staff that our 
daily school business has continued to be productive and 
positive. After all, our children really just want to be 
children! Unfortunately, they are exposed to a wider world 
that families and schools continue to partner around, in order 
to help them understand and cope. 
Our school mission highlights this joint partnering as a 
"learning community" with the essential ingredients 
of caring, communication and commitment Difficult 
times test every community while at the same time, re-
affirming our bonds and reassuring our children can be 
comforting. 
How can I discuss this with my child? 
On a practical level, it is helpful to focus on what our 
children do have control over, especially during times when 
they may be feeling vulnerable to external forces that they do 
not control. Encouraging our children to practice daily 
habits of positive care for themselves and all others, along 
with an expectation that if they see/hear something 
to communicate that to you and to us at school. When our 
children commit to doing their very best, at home and at 
school, it "drives up" our collective positive school culture! 
On a more conceptual level, please refer to the link below 
which offers further guidance around helping our children 
understand and cope with the wider world. 
httos://www.nasponline.oralresources-and-
publications/resources/school-safetv-and-crisis/talking-to-
children-about-violence-tips-for-parents-and-teachers 
What is the school's position on national school 
walkouts? 
Saxe has always acted as an apolitical, non-partisan public 
school. As such, we have not endorsed or participated in 
previous national march/protest days. However, we are 
proud of our past experiences supporting national days of 
honor and remembrance. 
As of this writing, there are two calls for national action on 
behalf of students in school. One has identified only high 
school participation; the other has been silent as to the age of 
EFTA_R1_01003859 
EFTA02237975
--- PAGE 3 ---
participants. One organization has planned for Wednesday 
March 14 and the other for Friday April 20. 
Links below: 
https://www.actionnetwork.org/event campaigns/enough-
national-school-walkout 
http://nationalschoolwalkout.us/ 
https://twitter.com/schoolwalkoutus?lang=en 
Saxe will continue to focus on giving our students 
appropriate channels to develop and express empathy, as 
well as, gratitude. Our recent "14 days of Kindness" 
campaign was led by San students in order to encourage 
everyone to add their portion of acceptance and positivity to 
the school culture. 
What is being planned at Sate on the days designated 
for student walkout? 
The Saxe administration is presently discussing a safe and 
student-centered approach for our school to appropriately 
express empathy for the victims of school violence, as well 
as, act with gratitude in order to increase the level of 
positive school culture as the spring semester progresses. 
Various 7th and 8th grade students are currently meeting 
with 7th grade administrator, Mr. Bedard and 8m grade 
administrator, Dr. Ferreira to formulate our approach. Once 
our plans are solidified, we will update all students and 
parents. 
What else can I do as a parent? 
Please use this email as a "springboard" to open up a 
conversation with your child. If our students understand that 
their family and school are in partnership in order to keep 
them safe and allow them the best environment to learn in, 
then they will, more likely, practice effective decision-
making. As we near the walkout dates, we will have some 
more detail to share about the planning that has resulted 
from our various student and parent inputs. 
We continue to remain available to you as your child's 
advocate. Please contact any member of our staff if you 
have a question or concern or just want reassurance. Our 
counselors and mental health staff are excellent resources in 
every school. Certainly if you see/hear something, please 
contact us so that we may arrange the necessary follow 
through. All of the reports from the Saxe staff, as well as, 
from our individual contacts with students, continue to 
indicate that our school community feels cared for and safe,

complex and challenging work of educating your middle 
school-aged child! 
With regards. 
Greg Maccdo

On Feb 6, 2018, at 12:21 PM, Natalia Molotkova 
wrote: 
Lesley, from my partner: can you run it by girls? Snowmass or Aspen? 
Aspen the town — or Snowmass? Snowmass is the major 'Aspen ski resort' — Aspen is the town. 
Snowmass is about 20 minutes away on convenient shuttle. With more ski in and out options. 
Most stay at Snowmass, then go to Aspen for shopping and dining. The ski hill in Aspen is 
smaller and steeper. If they are expert to intermediate skiers and are familiar with this type of 
terrain, then Aspen might be perfect. Otherwise I might recommend Snowmass. 
Lift ticket passes work for both Aspen, Snowmass and the two smaller hills in-between called 
Highlands and Buttermilk. But Snowmass is by far the larger ski area base with three village 
levels of shopping and dining. 
Rentals can be picked up at a conveniently located shop or delivered at the lodge. Skiers or 
snowboarders? Helmets or no helmets? 
Transportation from the airport is included in most Snowmass packages, but not Aspen. For 
Aspen we arrange e for a round trip shuttle/taxi.

On Feb 6, 2018, at 12:36 PM, Lesley Groff .:IM
E> wrote: 
Please see below and let me know your thoughts as soon as possible... 
Aspen the town — or Snowmass? Snowmass is the major 'Aspen ski resort' — Aspen is 
the town. Snowmass is about 20 minutes away on convenient shuttle. With more ski in 
and out options. Most stay at Snowmass, then go to Aspen for shopping and dining. 
The ski hill in Aspen is smaller and steeper. If they are expert to intermediate skiers and 
are familiar with this type of terrain, then Aspen might be perfect. Otherwise I might 
recommend Snowmass. 
Lift ticket passes work for both Aspen, Snowmass and the two smaller hills in-between 
called Highlands and Buttermilk. But Snowmass is by far the larger ski area base with 
three village levels of shopping and dining. 
Rentals can be picked up at a conveniently located shop or delivered at the lodge. Skiers 
or snowboarders? Helmets or no helmets? 
Transportation from the airport is included in most Snowmass packages, but not Aspen. 
For Aspen we arrange e for a round trip shuttle/taxi.

On Feb 6, 2018, at 12:36 PM, Lesley Groff 
wrote: 
Please see below and let me know your thoughts as soon as 
possible... 
Aspen the town — or Snowmass? Snowmass is the major 'Aspen ski resort' 
— Aspen is the town. Snowmass is about 20 minutes away on convenient 
shuttle. With more ski in and out options. Most stay at Snowmass, then 
go to Aspen for shopping and dining. The ski hill in Aspen is smaller and 
steeper. If they are expert to intermediate skiers and are familiar with this 
type of terrain, then Aspen might be perfect. Otherwise I might 
recommend Snowmass. 
Lift ticket passes work for both Aspen, Snowmass and the two smaller hills 
in-between called Highlands and Buttermilk. But Snowmass is by far the 
larger ski area base with three village levels of shopping and dining. 
Rentals can be picked up at a conveniently located shop or delivered at the 
lodge. Skiers or snowboarders? Helmets or no helmets? 
Transportation from the airport is included in most Snowmass packages, 
but not Aspen. For Aspen we arrange e for a round trip shuttle/taxi.
